gloss: the three essential New Year's dishes

definitions.gloss: the three essential New Year's dishes
definitions.explanation: The three symbolic dishes regarded as indispensable to {御節|おせち} New Year's cuisine. In eastern Japan they are {黒豆|くろまめ} (sweet black beans), {数|かず}の{子|こ} (herring roe), and {田作|たづく}り (candied dried sardines); in western Japan {田作|たづく}り is replaced by たたきごぼう (pounded burdock).

examples.japanese: {三|み}つ{肴|ざかな}だけは{必|かなら}ず{用意|ようい}する。
examples.english: We always prepare at least the three essential dishes.

examples.japanese: {関西|かんさい}の{三|み}つ{肴|ざかな}には たたきごぼう が{入|はい}る。
examples.english: The western Japanese version of the three dishes includes pounded burdock.

examples.japanese: {御節|おせち}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{作|つく}る{時間|じかん}はないので、{三|み}つ{肴|ざかな}と{雑煮|ぞうに}だけにした。
examples.english: We didn't have time to make a full osechi spread, so we settled for the three essential dishes and zoni soup.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三|み}つ{肴|ざかな}をそろえる: to assemble the three dishes
- {祝|いわ}い{肴|ざかな}{三種|さんしゅ}: the three celebratory dishes (formal synonym)
- {関東|かんとう}の{三|み}つ{肴|ざかな}: the eastern Japanese set

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
Each dish carries a wish: {黒豆|くろまめ} for health and diligence, {数|かず}の{子|こ} for many descendants, and {田作|たづく}り for an abundant harvest. Because these three alone are said to make a proper New Year's table, they are the minimum many households keep even when skipping the rest of the {御節|おせち}.
